Header:
Date: 2025-11-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Rahul Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Streampath Eng Mgr), Marcus Chen (Staff Eng), Priya Nair (Sec Lead), Samir Patel (CTO)
Recording: yes
Notes/Shared links referenced: https://redwood.app/quickstart-playbook (shared), Streampath internal: drive/streampath/inference-pilot, benchmark sheet: https://sheets.example.com/streampath-benchmarks (linked)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Quickstart walkthrough of Redwood SDK for Python + TypeScript, auth patterns (API key, SSO, KMS), sandbox provisioning, and integration checklist.
- Customer security questions about KMS/HSM, SOC 2 type II, network isolation (VPC), data retention, and audit logs.
- Agreement to run a 2-week pilot on Hosted with option to move to Dedicated depending on throughput/cost.

Topics: SDK install, env variables, API key rotation, KMS integration, VPC/private deployment, batching & prefix cache, sample call patterns, streaming vs non-streaming, rollout plan, success criteria.

Action items (captured during call): see metadata.action_items above.

Transcript body (timestamps are intermittent, transcription may have minor mis-words):
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, I'm the AE on this account, and Rahul is our solutions engineer. Quick intros and then we'll jump into the SDK faststart.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here — engineering manager for the data platform at Streampath. Marcus and Priya are on for the technicals. Samir might chime in later.
[00:25] Marcus Chen: Hey all.
[00:29] Priya Nair: Priya, security.
[00:32] Rahul Kapoor: Great to meet you. I can do a short live run where we install the SDK, show auth flows for both API-key and SSO, and provision a sandbox project. We'll also demo a basic generation, streaming, and an embeddings call.
[00:45] Samir Patel: Quick ask — we care about latency at 95th percentile and cost per 1k tokens. We'll want a baseline.
[00:52] Ava Martinez: Absolutely, we'll show where latency and cost levers live in the Console and how Optimize suggestions map to unit cost.
[01:05] Marcus Chen: What's the difference for us between starting Hosted vs Dedicated for a pilot? We want predictable throughput.
[01:12] Rahul Kapoor: Good question. Hosted is fastest to start, you get our managed runtime in minutes. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and throughput SLOs. For a short pilot — hosted with a reserved test window often works, then you can morph to Dedicated when you need consistent p95 SLA. Also, we can do a smoke benchmark to project cost.
[01:34] Priya Nair: Security — do you have SOC2 Type II? What about KMS integration, can we bring our own?
[01:40] Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for Hosted we integrate with cloud KMS and offer envelope encryption. We'll send the security pack after the call.
[01:55] Priya Nair: And audit logs and RBAC? We need per-user audit trails.
[01:59] Rahul Kapoor: Console has token-level tracing and audit logs. RBAC with SSO (SAML/SCIM) is supported — you can map groups to roles. We'll share a short doc on mapping SCIM groups to Console roles.
[02:20] Ava Martinez: Ok Rahul, want to kick off the SDK quickstart?
[02:24] Rahul Kapoor: Yep, hopping in. I'm going to share my screen — you should see a terminal. First, pip install redwood-inference-sdk — in Node it's npm i @redwood/inference. Then set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use the SSO flow via the Console.
[02:45] [screen share noise]
[02:48] Rahul Kapoor: Quick note, when people say K V cache or K-V cache in transcripts it's the KV cache for autoregeneration, we often see it mis-typed. The SDK exposes prefix cache helpers for session-based reuse.
[03:05] Marcus Chen: That prefix cache — any auto-eviction policies?
[03:09] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, you can configure eviction by size and TTL in the Console or programmatically via the SDK. In Dedicated, caches can be pinned per-tenant for lower cold-starts.
[03:25] [04:00] Rahul Kapoor: Example python call: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); resp = c.generate(model='rw-xl-1', prompt='summarize...') — streaming is available via resp.stream().
[04:22] Lena Ortiz: Do you have typed response objects? We want strong typing in TypeScript.
[04:26] Rahul Kapoor: TS SDK returns typed interfaces out of the box, plus helper types for function calling. We also auto-generate model profiles so your infra can switch models with minimal code changes.
[04:40] [04:58] Priya Nair: What's the recommended key rotation cadence and how do you handle secrets in CI?
[05:04] Ava Martinez: We recommend rotating keys every 90 days. For CI use short-lived tokens via the Console or use workload identity/IRSA (GCP, AWS) to avoid long-lived secrets. We'll include example GitHub Actions and GitLab examples in the playbook.
[05:25] Marcus Chen: For embeddings, we plan to embed customer transcripts. Need to know about retention and redaction.
[05:31] Rahul Kapoor: By default we don't surface customer data to other tenants. For Hosted we offer configurable retention windows and opt-out. For Private deployments you fully control retention and can enable automatic redaction.
[05:46] [06:10] Rahul Kapoor: Now provisioning a sandbox: we create a project in the Console, assign an API key, enable a sandbox model (we have curated small models for fast dev). You can also request a dev-only VPC if you need network isolation.
[06:28] Lena Ortiz: That dev VPC — is it available for Hosted?
[06:31] Rahul Kapoor: Hosted supports customer VPC peering in some regions. For full network isolation and on-prem policy you'd look at Private deployment. We'll capture details in the security doc.
[06:45] [07:00] Marcus Chen: Any gotchas with our infra? We're largely on k8s/eks with private subnets.
[07:06] Rahul Kapoor: We commonly integrate via private endpoints or peering. In our experience you need to open specific egress to model-serving endpoints or set up a proxy. We'll share step-by-step eks examples.
[07:23] [07:45] Rahul Kapoor: Alright, I'm going to demo an end-to-end quickstart: create project, generate a call, show streaming, then an embedding and a small rerank.
[07:50] [08:10] Rahul Kapoor: (typing) Creating project "streampath-dev" — done. Generating with model "rw-4-small" — here we get a 120ms p50 locally — keep in mind hosted p95 may be higher. Streaming example now...
[08:32] Marcus Chen: That p50 number — how hard is it to reproduce on our side?
[08:36] Rahul Kapoor: Depends on prompt size, tokenization, batch settings. We'll run a small benchmark script that sends a representative mix and returns p50/p95 and token cost. We have a benchmark template in the shared sheet.
[08:52] Priya Nair: For the benchmark, can we run it inside our VPC?
[08:56] Ava Martinez: If you have a private peering set up we can run the benchmark against Hosted endpoints via the private link. For Dedicated or Private we run it within their environment.
[09:10] Marcus Chen: How does batching affect latency? If we batch to save cost, we could hurt p95.
[09:16] Rahul Kapoor: Exactly — it's a tradeoff. Optimize suggests batching configs based on your QPS and latency SLOs. You can set per-route policies: e.g., conversational routes can be low-latency with small batch sizes, background embedding routes can be larger.
[09:34] [10:00] Rahul Kapoor: Next, auth: example Node snippet: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); // or use client.loginSSO({redirectUrl}) for SSO. We also show how to mint short-lived session tokens via the Console for CI.
[10:20] Priya Nair: For SSO, do you support SCIM auto-provisioning?
[10:24] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, SCIM for user provisioning and SAML for login. Group-to-role mappings are configurable. We'll send a sample SAML metadata file and SCIM mappings.
[10:40] Samir Patel: If we need to go on-prem later, what's the pattern for model updates and kernel optimizations?
[10:48] Rahul Kapoor: For Private on-prem we ship an appliance/package and an updater to pull validated model versions; kernel selection and quantization profiles are configurable. We maintain a compiled kernel catalog that maps to hardware.
[11:05] Marcus Chen: You mentioned KV cache pinning for Dedicated — can you explain that again?
[11:09] Rahul Kapoor: KV cache pinning keeps session caches resident on the same GPU pool to reduce warmup. For high-throughput conversational workloads it reduces tail latency.
[11:25] [11:50] Rahul Kapoor: Switching to TypeScript quickstart — I'll open the repo. npm i @redwood/inference; create a .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID. Example usage: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'; const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const res = await c.chat.create({ messages: [{role:'user', content:'Summarize...'}] }); console.log(res.choices[0].message.content);
[12:12] Lena Ortiz: Error handling patterns? We want to handle transient errors and fallbacks gracefully.
[12:16] Rahul Kapoor: SDK exposes retryable error codes; we recommend exponential backoff with jitter. Also use automatic fallback policies in the Console to route to a cheaper or smaller model on overload.
[12:34] Priya Nair: Will fallback expose data to other model variants?
[12:38] Ava Martinez: Fallbacks stay within the customer's project and tenancy. If you route to a different model family, it's still within the same privacy boundaries. For multi-tenant Hosted, we ensure tenant isolation.
[12:55] [13:20] Marcus Chen: For observability, can we tag calls from different services?
[13:24] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, you can pass metadata/labels on each request. Console dashboards can filter by tag, model, route, and token cost.
[13:38] Lena Ortiz: Great. Can we show cost per route in Console?
[13:41] Ava Martinez: Yep. Console breaks down token cost by route, model, and per-token breakdown with trend lines. Optimize will also suggest quantization or smaller models for cost saving.
[13:58] Rahul Kapoor: I'm switching to the Console now to show the Optimize suggestions UI — here's a workload that is embedding-heavy; Optimize suggests int8 quantization and a different batching profile saving ~35% unit cost.
[14:26] Priya Nair: Are those suggestions automated or just advisory?
[14:29] Rahul Kapoor: Advisory by default. You can opt into automatic rollout of those changes for non-critical routes. For critical routes you can do canary rollouts.
[14:44] [15:05] Marcus Chen: One blocker: our procurement wants a data processing addendum and liability limits. Who handles that?
[15:10] Ava Martinez: Our legal team will share standard DPA and SLAs. For enterprise agreements, we can negotiate terms. I'll start that thread once you confirm intent to pilot.
[15:28] Priya Nair: Anything specific about encryption at rest and in transit?
[15:32] Rahul Kapoor: TLS for in transit, encryption at rest via cloud KMS by default; BYOK is available for Private. HSM-backed keys can be integrated for an extra compliance layer.
[15:50] [16:10] Rahul Kapoor: Now, quick live embedding run: I'm sending a sample doc, generating embedding, then storing to an in-memory vector store to show recall. (typing) embedding vector length 1,536 for rw-embed-xl.
[16:30] Marcus Chen: That vector size — what's indexing recommendation?
[16:34] Rahul Kapoor: For 1,536 dims use HNSW for low-latency approximate nearest neighbor; for large corpora we recommend product quantization layers. We have a small guide in the playbook.
[16:50] [17:15] Lena Ortiz: For the pilot, we want to measure p95 under load. What dataset do you recommend?
[17:19] Rahul Kapoor: Use a representative mix of short chat prompts and longer summarization prompts. We'll share a benchmark harness that supports ramp and constant QPS.
[17:35] Priya Nair: For the pilot, what's the default retention of logs?
[17:39] Ava Martinez: By default Hosted retains logs 30 days; Console has adjustable retention and long-term export to your storage. For enterprise we can increase retention windows.
[17:55] [18:20] Rahul Kapoor: Quick aside — some transcription systems mix up product names; occasionally 'Redwood Console' shows up as 'Redwood counsel' in exports, so apologies if the auto-summary has weird words.
[18:37] Marcus Chen: Ha, noted.
[18:40] [19:00] Rahul Kapoor: Ok next section — CI/CD secrets examples: I'll show a GitHub Action snippet that fetches a short-lived token from the Console via an API and uses it to call generate. We recommend against baking long-lived REDWOOD_API_KEY into repos.
[19:20] Lena Ortiz: Can the short-lived tokens be scoped per-route?
[19:23] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, tokens can be scoped and time-limited. Good for least-privilege.
[19:40] [20:00] Priya Nair: From a compliance POV, does Console provide exportable audit logs?
[20:04] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, audit logs exportable to S3/GCS or pushed to SIEM via webhooks. We'll include a sample config for Splunk/Datadog.
[20:22] Marcus Chen: Let's talk SLO targets — what's typical for p95 on Hosted?
[20:26] Rahul Kapoor: Depends on model. Smaller models can hit sub-200ms p95 for short prompts; larger models will be higher. Dedicated gives you control to hit a specific p95 with reserved GPU capacity.
[20:45] [21:10] Ava Martinez: I want to capture rough pilot plan: two-week Hosted pilot with 3 routes (chat low-latency, summarization medium-latency, embeddings background); run benchmark day 2, review metrics day 7, decide on Dedicated vs continue Hosted by day 14. Thoughts?
[21:28] Lena Ortiz: That sounds reasonable. We'll confirm internal owners and the success criteria (p95 < 700ms for chat, cost per 1k tokens <$X).
[21:40] Samir Patel: Agree, also include security sign-off.
[21:44] [22:05] Rahul Kapoor: Great — I'll add the pilot steps to the playbook and share.
[22:12] [22:30] Marcus Chen: A small nit: how to keep embeddings deterministic across quant upgrades?
[22:34] Rahul Kapoor: For embeddings we version the model; quantization changes are documented per model version. We recommend pinning an embedding model version in production.
[22:50] [23:10] Priya Nair: How are anomalies detected? We need alerts when quality drops.
[23:14] Rahul Kapoor: Console supports quality monitor tied to prompt sets/seed evaluations and can alert on regressions. You can upload golden prompt sets to track drift.
[23:34] Ava Martinez: Ok quick Q and A session — please call out any blockers.
[23:40] Lena Ortiz: Blocker: procurement wants vendor security questionnaire answered.
[23:44] Ava Martinez: We'll send completed vendor security package; Rahul will help with details.
[23:52] Marcus Chen: Blocker: we need a reproducible test harness to run inside our environment.
[23:56] Rahul Kapoor: We'll share the harness repo and a dockerized runner.
[24:10] [24:30] Rahul Kapoor: Time check — we have about 24 minutes left to do a deeper demo if you want, like a small canary rollout.
[24:36] Lena Ortiz: Can we go through SSO setup briefly? That's top of mind.
[24:40] Rahul Kapoor: Sure — SSO setup: in Console > Org Settings > SSO, paste your SAML metadata, map attributes, enable SCIM for user sync. After initial setup, you can test with a single user before org-wide enforcement.
[25:02] Priya Nair: Will SCIM support our Azure AD groups?
[25:06] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, Azure AD is supported.
[25:12] [25:35] Rahul Kapoor: Now a short canary demo: create a route, set a canary of 10% to new model, monitor logs and error rates, then ramp. This prevents wholesale regressions.
[25:52] Marcus Chen: Is function/tool calling supported? We need to call internal tools from the model.
[25:56] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, the SDK supports structured function calling and tool hooks; you can register type-safe tool schemas in the Console.
[26:10] [26:40] Rahul Kapoor: Ok switching to a quick failure scenario: if the primary model is overloaded we can fallback to a cheaper smaller model automatically; fallbacks are policy driven and you can set thresholds.
[26:54] Lena Ortiz: Will fallback increase cost unexpectedly?
[26:58] Rahul Kapoor: Fallback usually reduces cost; it's meant to preserve availability. But you should monitor quality regressions.
[27:12] [27:30] Samir Patel: Are there reference customers in fintech for this stack?
[27:34] Ava Martinez: Yes, we have refs. I'll share a short case study that matches your compliance profile.
[27:44] [28:00] Rahul Kapoor: Wrapping up the tech demo portion — I'm uploading the sample code and the playbook link in the chat now.
[28:10] [28:30] Rahul Kapoor: (chat message posted) link: https://redwood.app/playbooks/streampath-quickstart — contains: install steps, snippets, CI examples, SSO/SCIM template, benchmark harness, and security pack.
[28:48] Priya Nair: Thanks. Quick question: for audit log retention to our S3 bucket, is that push or pull?
[28:53] Rahul Kapoor: We can push logs to your bucket or provide exports you can pull. Push via event sink is supported.
[29:10] [29:35] Lena Ortiz: How long to set up a dev sandbox end-to-end if we grant access now?
[29:40] Ava Martinez: With access we can provision a sandbox in under an hour; SSO and private peering will take longer — typically 2–3 days for SSO and a week for network config depending on your infra teams.
[30:00] Marcus Chen: Any quotas we should know about for trial?
[30:04] Rahul Kapoor: For pilots we increase quota; we'll set a baseline QPS for the trial and will scale if needed.
[30:18] [30:42] Rahul Kapoor: Demo done — now lightning Qs.
[30:46] Priya Nair: Does Redwood support on-prem GPU scheduling if we host Private?
[30:50] Rahul Kapoor: Yes, we support on-prem scheduler integrations and can coordinate driver/kernel versions.
[31:04] Marcus Chen: Can we sandbox policy for model outputs? We want profanity and PII filters.
[31:08] Rahul Kapoor: We have pre-routing filters and post-routing content filters and a configurable redaction pipeline.
[31:24] [31:50] Lena Ortiz: Will you be able to provide a test account for our bench team?
[31:54] Ava Martinez: Yes, we'll provide a sandbox with credentials and a preloaded dataset for the bench team.
[32:10] Rahul Kapoor: Also note the SDK has a local dev mode that mocks calls for unit tests.
[32:20] Marcus Chen: Nice.
[32:34] [33:00] Rahul Kapoor: Quick performance note: if you push quantized int8 kernels you reduce memory and cost but check for small deltas in downstream embedding similarity measurements.
[33:16] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Anything else on security?
[33:20] Priya Nair: One more: do you support Customer-managed HSM?
[33:24] Rahul Kapoor: Yes for Private, and enterprise Hosted customers can arrange HSM with contractual terms.
[33:36] [34:00] Ava Martinez: We're nearing time. Quick recap and next steps? Rahul want to run through owners.
[34:06] Rahul Kapoor: Sure. Rahul: send sandbox playbook, harness repo, and eks peering steps by 2025-11-28. Ava: send pricing, DPA template, and case study by 2025-11-29. Streampath (Lena): confirm pilot owners and target success criteria by 2025-12-01.
[34:30] Lena Ortiz: We'll do that. Also, request procurement to schedule call with your legal early next week.
[34:36] Samir Patel: I'll be on that call.
[34:40] [35:00] Marcus Chen: One final technical ask: can you provide an example of a canary rollout config?
[35:04] Rahul Kapoor: I'll add one to the playbook.
[35:15] [35:30] Ava Martinez: Any other blockers?
[35:34] Lena Ortiz: None from me.
[35:36] Priya Nair: No.
[35:38] [36:00] Rahul Kapoor: Thanks all — we'll follow up.
[36:06] Ava Martinez: Thank you everyone.
[36:10] [36:30] Post-call notes (auto):
- Customer is aligned to a Hosted 2-week pilot with benchmark day 2 and review at week 1.
- Security pack and playbook to be shared; legal thread to be started.
- Next sync tentatively scheduled for 2025-12-02 to review benchmark results.
